newsitem.title: MAURITIUS: Long position firms Mauritius rupee versus dollar.
newsitem.headline: Long position firms Mauritius rupee versus dollar.

text.p: The Mauritian rupee firmed against both the dollar and pound on Thursday with a long position in the forex market seen overriding overnight international trends, forex dealers said.
The rupee was posted at a mean rate of 19.871 for one dollar, slightly firmer than 19.873 on Wednesday. Against the pound, it traded at a mean of 33.6525 on Thursday from 33.7025 on Wednesday.
Forex dealers said despite the dollar strengthening in overnight international markets, the rupee was fixed slightly firmer against the greenback because of a long position in the forex market.
"The long position means a wish to sell (dollars) and this has driven the rate of the dollar slightly down," said one dealer from an international bank.
The dealer added importers' forex demand had still not picked up from its year-end lull.
"On the other hand, presently there is quite a good (forex) supply from textiles exports and the tourism sector."
Together with sugar exports, textiles and tourism are the leading hard currency earners for Mauritius.
